Read .planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-HANDOVER-package-review.md first —
it has the detail behind everything below. Then read docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-
package-convergence.md.

DO NOT PUSH until I say so. Do not touch the pc1/pc2 VMs or the Hetzner lock unasked. Ask when using pc1/pc2 would be useful for analysis.

OPEN WORK, in priority order. Organize your work. You orchestrate. Use todo-list. Sub-agents do the work (both analysis, code and doc):

1. The apt no-candidate detector has never fired. _packages_with_no_candidate (copies in
    manual_installs_sync.py and apt_sync.py) tests for literal "Candidate: (none)", which
    apt does NOT print for a hand-installed .deb — dpkg's status entry supplies the
    candidate. Verified: code, brscan3, cnpg, falco-app, brother-udev-rule-type1 all report
    a version. Correct test is already in the codebase: installed version whose only origin
    is /var/lib/dpkg/status (reuse _installed_origins_by_package from 43a52fa3).

2. Derived repos — designed and approved by me, not started. apt sources stop being
    independently reviewable, exactly as keys did in d27337da: adding a repo is derived
    from the packages approved from it, the repo is named in the package's review detail,
    removal stays reviewed, and /etc/apt/sources.list + ubuntu.sources are NEVER collected.
    Follow d27337da for shape and 43a52fa3 for naming consequences in `detail`.

3. The batched review has never been driven by a human. Unit tests inject a FakeReviewer
    (tests/unit/jobs/test_package_sync_core.py:72 and test_manual_installs_sync.py:132);
    the VM suite bypasses prompting entirely via PCSWITCHER_PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION
    (src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py:94). So decisions are proven; prompts are not.
    Nothing has ever rendered a questionary checkbox, paused/resumed the Rich Live panel
    around one, driven the multi-line snippet editor, or hit Ctrl-C at a prompt.
    Worst case: commit 089ea985 added a SECOND review that fires mid-execute(), after
    /etc/apt converges (apt_sync.py:1410-1441). Untested at every level.
    02-UAT.md test 1 covers this and is still pending. I want to run it myself — give me
    copy-paste commands, don't drive it for me.

RULES THAT COST US PREVIOUS SESSIONS:
- Insist on RED. A test that cannot fail is not a test. Treat SKIPPED as not-a-test. When
  retrofitting tests onto existing code (no red phase available), mutation-check instead:
  break the implementation, confirm the test fails, restore.
- Tests create the environment they need. No discover-or-skip. No pytest.skip in
  tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py. Fixtures live in
  tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh.
- Subagents experiment in docker or on pc1/pc2, never on this dev machine.
- Verify before asserting. Check this machine rather than describing how software
  "usually" behaves.

DO NOT RE-LITIGATE (verified on real VMs): #208 D9 holds; the #215 flatpak GPG trust fix
survives real Flathub; keyring resolution went 11 dangling -> 0; snap refresh.hold needs
sudo to read (5e6a9a4c, pushed).
I'll start by reading the handover and ADR, then organize the work.

16	## 1. The review has never been driven by a human — highest priority
17	
18	The batched review is the phase's whole interaction surface and **no test drives the real one**. Unit tests inject a fake; the VM suite sets an env var that bypasses prompting entirely. Nobody has watched it render.

20	Where things are:
21

25	| Constructed | `src/pcswitcher/orchestrator.py:394` |

Untested end to end: questionary checkbox rendering, pause/resume of the Rich Live panel around each prompt, the second "never offer again on this machine?" checkbox, the unreproducible three-way resolution with its multi-line snippet editor, the collateral install-anyway/skip/abort prompt, and Ctrl-C/EOF aborting the whole sync from each of those.

35	## 2. Derived repos — designed and approved, not started
36	
37	User decision: apt sources stop being independently reviewable items, exactly as keys did in `d27337da`.
38	
39	- Adding a repo is **derived** from the packages approved from it — no separate tickable line. This makes "package ticked, its source unticked" unrepresentable, which is where a family of inconsistencies came from.
40	- The repo is **named in the package's review detail** ("install gh (adds repo cli.github.com)") so the system change is visible without being a separate decision.
41	- Removal stays reviewed — it is destructive and affects packages that remain.
42	- **`/etc/apt/sources.list` and `ubuntu.sources` are never collected.** Reference counting protects them in practice (`ubuntu.sources` maps to 126 manual packages on the user's machine) but that must not be load-bearing on a delete.
43	
44	Rationale is settled: the user only ever adds a repo because they want a package from it, so repo lifecycle is derivable from package lifecycle. Precedent to follow: `d27337da` (keys) for the shape, `43a52fa3` for naming consequences in `detail`.
45

48	## 3. The no-candidate detector has never fired
49	
50	`_packages_with_no_candidate` (copies in `src/pcswitcher/jobs/manual_installs_sync.py` and `src/pcswitcher/jobs/apt_sync.py`) tests for the literal `Candidate: (none)`. **apt does not print that for a package installed from a hand-downloaded `.deb`** — dpkg's own status entry supplies the candidate.
51	
52	Measured on the user's machine: `code`, `brscan3`, `cnpg`, `falco-app`, `brother-udev-rule-type1` all report `Candidate: <installed version>`. The detector matches none of them, so `manual_installs_sync`'s primary detection finds nothing, no snippet is ever offered, and `apt_sync` proposes those packages as ordinary installs that fail on the target with "Unable to locate package".
53	
54	D-18's calibration ("4 apt packages have no repo candidate on P17") came from a rule that does not match reality.
55	
56	Correct test, already implemented for C26 in `43a52fa3`: a package whose installed version's **only origin is `/var/lib/dpkg/status`** came from no repo. `gh` shows `500 https://cli.github.com/packages` alongside it; `code` shows only the dpkg line. Reuse `_installed_origins_by_package`.
57	
58	Note: with the second review now in place, a package this fix reclassifies gets re-diffed after `apt-get update`, so a `(none)` → available transition reaches the user the same run.
59	
60	## 4. Smaller open items
61	
62	- **A pin on the target makes a package un-removable and un-markable.** The pinned branch in `sync_core.py` `_diff_apt_packages` requires only `target_item is not None`, so a package present on the target, absent from the source and named by any pin never produces a `REMOVE` item — and `REPORT_ONLY` items cannot be skip-always'd, so the noise cannot be silenced either. No decision covers suppressing the *removal* direction. Needs a user ruling.
63	- **Same package surfaced by two managers** (`apt_sync` `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` + `manual_installs_sync` unreproducible) — matrix A11, no test, never decided.
64	- **Dry-run shows the pre-repository classification**, since it converges nothing and so cannot re-review. Documented in `apt_sync`'s module docstring and `docs/jobs/package-sync.md`.
65	- **flatpak twin of the contradictory pair** (matrix F9): `_remote_ready_on_target` answers from plan-time state, so an approved remote *removal* plus an approved ref install from it slips the guard.
66	
67	## 5. Verified this session — do not re-litigate
68	
69	- #208 D9 **holds**: a system-wide `refresh.hold` does not mask per-snap `held` notes. Proven on a VM once the privileged-read fix landed.
70	- The #215 flatpak GPG trust fix **survives real Flathub** — options parse, keyring digest read, `--gpg-import` reproducing a byte-identical keyring, and the replicated remote actually installing.
71	- Keyring resolution: **11 of 20 source files dangling → 0**, re-verified independently against the real `/etc/apt`.
72	- `snap get system refresh.hold` is admin-gated; the unprivileged read returned `None` unconditionally, which made every sync clear a user's own hold. Fixed in `5e6a9a4c` (pushed).
73

76	- **Three vacuous tests shipped this phase** before being caught: the seven discover-or-skip VM tests, `test_snap_revision_converges_without_hold`, and `test_key_then_source_then_update_then_package_install`. All three passed while proving nothing. Mutation-check anything load-bearing — break the implementation, confirm the test fails.
77	- **Tests must create the environment they need.** There is no discover-or-skip convention any more; `tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh` provisions snaps and real Flathub into the VM baseline. No `pytest.skip` belongs in `tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py`.
78	- **Agents experiment in docker or on pc1/pc2, never the dev machine.** One removed user flatpak state here.
79	- The VM lock (`tests/integration/scripts/internal/lock.sh`) leaks on a CI timeout and needs `clear` by hand. The user accepts this; timeouts are the thing to prevent.
80	- Integration CI only triggers on PRs targeting `main`.

1	# ADR-020: Declarative package convergence: manifest capture, item diff, replay via each ecosystem's own tooling
2	
3	Status: Accepted
4	
5	Date: 2026-07-23
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	The source captures a manifest of package-related items (apt/snap/flatpak packages, repos, pins, config, remotes, blocks); the target diffs its own state against it and converges using `apt`, `snap` and `flatpak` themselves — package databases are never rsynced. Four independent jobs (`apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync`, `manual_installs_sync`) each run plan then review then apply inside their own `execute()`, and each reviews its own items — batched per manager and grouped by action — before that job issues its first mutating command.
10	
11	## Implementation Rules
12	
13	**Required:**
14	- `/var/lib/dpkg`, `/var/lib/snapd` and the flatpak OSTree store MUST NOT be rsynced or otherwise file-mirrored; convergence happens only through `apt`, `snap` and `flatpak` invocations.
15	- Every handled thing (package, source, pin, config file, block, snap, snap channel, flatpak ref, flatpak remote, unreproducible install) MUST be modeled as an `Item` with a stable identity flowing through one diff → decide → apply pipeline.
16	- `apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync` and `manual_installs_sync` MUST be four separate `SyncJob`s, each with its own enable flag, validation, progress reporting and `JobResult` — never merged into one `package_sync` job. `manual_installs_sync` MUST carry its own `sync_jobs` enable flag so disabling apt cannot silently disable manual-install detection.
17	- Each package job MUST review an item before issuing any command that changes it; the plan → review → apply sequence lives inside that job's own `execute()`. Reviews SHOULD be batched — one screen per manager per action — and a job MUST NOT prompt per item where a batch would do. A job MAY review again when this run's own changes invalidate the facts an earlier review was answered on; correctness outranks the batching preference.
18	- The `/etc/apt` convergence group MUST be transactional: a group whose metadata refresh fails MUST leave the target's `/etc/apt` as it found it.
19	- A package manager's own transaction MUST be constrained to what the review approved: what it would change beyond the approved item is determined at plan time and classified there, never prompted mid-apply.
20	- Machine-local decision files MUST live at `~/.config/pc-switcher/<manager>.decisions.yaml`, one per manager, excluded from `folder_sync` non-overridably and outside `config_sync`.
21	- Whether an unreproducible item counts as reproducible MUST be judged by whether the SOURCE holds a snippet, never by whether the target already does. The install-snippet registry (`~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml`) MUST be pushed to the target by `manual_installs_sync` itself and replayed there the same run — including a snippet authored on the fly during that run's review. A push that would lose or change an entry only the target holds MUST require explicit confirmation and abort the run when it cannot get it. `config_sync` MUST NOT carry the registry.
22	
23	**Forbidden:**
24	- No `--delete` file mirror of `/etc/apt` or any other package-database directory.
25	- No component outside a package job may own that job's review; the review call stays inside the job's own `execute()`.
26	- No standing block on a package manager's own auto-update left behind by a run. A transient guard across the sync window is allowed if it is restored on cleanup and self-expires (D-06).
27	- No re-fetching signing keys from vendors; a repo's key travels with its repo, byte-for-byte.
28	
29	## Context
30	
31	Phase 2 must replicate presence, version and provenance of packages across apt, snap and flatpak, plus the repository/keyring/pin/remote configuration those installs depend on. Package data under `~/.var/app`, `~/snap/<app>/common` and dotfiles is already Phase 1 `folder_sync` territory; this ADR concerns the packages themselves and the `/etc/apt` config that governs where they come from.
32	
33	The review boundary is the manager: each package job captures its own diff and surfaces it for an explicit decision before it applies anything, and no review spans more than a single manager's items. This keeps four deliberately independent jobs independent — each owns its own capture, review, apply, failure isolation and progress — rather than binding them to a shared review that would give them a common ordering and failure surface.
34	
35	## Decision
36	
37	### Convergence model (D-01)
38	
39	The source captures a manifest; the target diffs its own state against it and converges using `apt`, `snap` and `flatpak` themselves. `/var/lib/dpkg`, `/var/lib/snapd` and the flatpak OSTree store are never rsynced — the package managers stay authoritative for their own state.
40	
41	### Item model (D-02)
42	
43	Every handled thing is an item with a stable identity, not just packages: apt package, apt source, apt pin, apt config file, apt hold, snap, snap channel, snap hold, flatpak ref, flatpak remote, flatpak mask, unreproducible/manual install. All classes flow through one diff → decide → apply pipeline.
44	
45	Item granularity follows what the user can meaningfully decide about. Standing user intent gets its own identity even when it is attached to something else: a deliberate block on a package (apt hold, snap hold, flatpak mask) is a decision in its own right and replicates as its own item, separate from the package it applies to. Mechanism the user has no basis to judge is not an item and is the job's own business to keep correct. A transient guard a run sets and clears is not an item either.
46	
47	### Manifest content for apt (D-03)
48	
49	The manifest carries the manually-installed set from `apt-mark showmanual`, not the full dpkg selection set; apt resolves dependencies on the target.
50	
51	### Version policy (D-04, D-05)
52	
53	Versions float to whatever the target's repos currently offer; version mismatch is a reported diff class, never a forced downgrade. This float-only policy is apt and flatpak. Snap is the deliberate exception: it converges revision and channel (D-06), because snap is the only ecosystem that embeds the version in its per-user data path (`~/snap/<app>/<rev>`), so keeping both machines on the same revision is what lets `folder_sync` mirror that data cleanly. Deliberate pinning replicates because `/etc/apt/preferences.d` entries are items.
54	
55	### Revision/scope convergence (D-06)
56	
57	The snap manifest carries name + channel + revision; the flatpak manifest carries ref + origin + user/system scope. Snap convergence pins a revision explicitly and must never leave a snap blocked from auto-refresh once a run ends.
58	
59	snapd auto-refreshes in the background (~4×/day, even for closed apps), which could move a snap off the converged revision mid-run and desync the data dir `folder_sync` is mirroring. The orchestrator therefore pauses snapd's automatic refresh across the whole sync window on BOTH hosts, restoring each host's prior setting on cleanup and relying on a timeout so a crashed run does not leave the pause behind. This gates only the auto-refresh manager, not the explicit revision convergence.
60	
61	### Three-way decision and direction (D-07)
62	
63	Every actionable item gets a three-way decision: apply / skip once / skip always. "Apply" is direction-dependent — missing on target means install/add/enable, extra on target means remove/delete/disable, different on both means change the target to match the source. The review names the concrete action per item (e.g. "remove brscan3", not "apply").
64	
65	Report-only diffs (version mismatch, no repository candidate, held/pinned echo) offer apply or skip only. They carry no converge verb, so there is no holder machine for D-08a to record a permanent decision on, and recording one would suppress the item entirely rather than stop reporting the drift the user meant. They are resolved by fixing the underlying condition.
66	
67	### Machine-local decision file (D-08, D-08a, D-09, D-10)
68	
69	One file per manager lives at `~/.config/pc-switcher/<manager>.decisions.yaml`, never synced, excluded from `folder_sync` non-overridably and outside `config_sync`. An entry on machine M makes the item inert on M in both roles — not pushed when M is the source, not installed or removed when M is the target. The entry is written on the end of the connection that holds the item: source-held item declined is recorded on the source, target-held item whose removal is declined is recorded on the target.
70	
71	### Repository configuration as items (D-11, D-12, D-13)
72	
73	apt sources, pins, apt config, flatpak remotes and snap channels are inventory items, not a file mirror; a `--delete` mirror of `/etc/apt` would wipe the target's own machine-specific sources. Both `/etc/apt/preferences.d` and `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` sync as items. A flatpak remote's identity includes its URL as well as its name and scope, so a remote that moved converges rather than diverging silently.
74	
75	A repository's signing key travels with the repository, byte-for-byte from the source machine, and is never re-fetched from a vendor: the target must end up trusting exactly what the source trusts, and a fresh fetch would silently substitute whatever the vendor serves today. A repository whose key cannot be made to work on the target is reported rather than written.
76	
77	### Job split into four jobs (D-15, D-16, D-17, D-18)
78	
79	Four jobs — `apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync` and `manual_installs_sync` — over one shared core extracted while building, not deferred to a post-hoc refactor. The core is what all four use: the item taxonomy, the plan/review/apply order, the three-way decision flow, the batched TUI review and the machine-local file I/O. Each manager's own item shapes and its own diff stay in that manager's module — one manager's diff on the shared base would make the other three inherit inputs they never supply, which is the coupling D-15 exists to prevent. Package jobs run before `folder_sync` so apps are provisioned before their data lands (decisive for flatpak, where `~/.local/share/flatpak` must exist before `~/.var/app` arrives).
80	
81	`manual_installs_sync` owns everything no package manager can reproduce: the apt-no-candidate set and the scan for unowned installs under `/usr/local` and `/opt`, plus the snippet registry.
82	
83	### Per-manager review, batched by preference (D-15 + D-24)
84	
85	Each package job runs plan then review then apply inside its own `execute()`, and only converges diffs that review approved. Grouping by action matters because "apply" is direction-dependent (D-07): installs and removals show as separate groups, removals labelled as removals, so a bulk tick can never silently delete.
86	
87	Three properties are absolute. Nothing changes before it has been reviewed. No review spans two managers — the jobs are independent by D-15, so a single owner reviewing every enabled manager at once would contradict that independence, which is why there is no shared review phase and no coordinator. And a job never degrades a batch into a per-item question queue.
88	
89	Batching itself is a strong preference, not a fixed count: one screen per manager per action is the norm and the shape to design for, but a job MAY review again when correctness requires it — `apt_sync` converges `/etc/apt` before packages, so a pin the user deleted or a repository they installed changes what the package diff should have said. Asking twice is worse than asking once; asking once and being wrong is worse than both. Approvals the new state contradicts are withdrawn without asking, since dropping work needs no decision.
90	
91	### Transactional repository convergence (D-27 boundary)
92	
93	The `/etc/apt` group is the one place D-27's continue-and-report model does not apply: it is transactional, and a group whose metadata refresh fails leaves `/etc/apt` as it found it. Continuing past a bad write would leave the target's package manager unusable, and automatic snapshot rollback does not arrive until Phase 7.
94	
95	### apt transaction fidelity (D-30)
96	
97	apt may remove or downgrade packages other than the one named in order to satisfy dependencies, so the item the user ticked is not necessarily the transaction apt will run. The transaction is therefore determined at plan time and its collateral classified rather than blanket-refused, which would block a legitimate install whose only collateral is a dependency nobody chose: collateral apt pulled in on its own proceeds, while collateral that is manually installed on EITHER machine is something the user chose to have and becomes its own reviewable item offering install-anyway / skip / abort. Checking the source's manual set as well as the target's covers the package the user chose on the source but that arrives as collateral on the target. The question belongs in the review, never mid-apply — a prompt during apply reintroduces the prompt-flooding the batched review exists to prevent, and violates review-before-any-change.
98	
99	### Unreproducible items and where a run terminates (D-21 with D-26 and D-27)
100	
101	An unreproducible item ends a run resolved in one of three ways: it has a snippet, it is recorded machine-specific (skip-always), or the user chose to skip it once. Skip-once is a real decision, not an unresolved state — the user may be declining something temporary, and a run where they made that choice is clean. pc-switcher offers to add a snippet on the fly during the review, so resolving an item never requires leaving the sync. In an interactive review the "unresolved" outcome is unrepresentable, and abandoning the review aborts the whole sync rather than manufacturing a skip-once. Only a non-interactive run leaves items undecided; it does not fail on undecided items alone, because the user was never given the chance to resolve them (D-26).
102	
103	### Unreproducible items and snippets (D-18 through D-23)
104	
105	Detection covers no-repo-candidate apt packages and unowned installs under `/usr/local` and `/opt`, and is owned by `manual_installs_sync`. An install snippet is an opaque text blob replayed non-interactively through the existing executor with the exit code deciding success — the tool never parses, versions, diffs or reasons about snippet content. Snippets live in the shared, synced config (`~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml`) and cover bare `.deb`s and manual installs only; snap and flatpak items do not carry snippets (YAGNI — every current one comes from a reachable remote).
106	
107	Whether an item counts as reproducible is decided by whether the SOURCE — the machine being replicated — holds a snippet, never by whether the target already does. `manual_installs_sync` pushes the registry to the target itself and replays it the same run, so a snippet authored on the fly during that run's review takes effect immediately rather than next run. The push is a wholesale overwrite gated on being non-destructive: one that would lose or change an entry only the target holds needs explicit confirmation, so a snippet the user only has on the target is never silently discarded. The registry does not travel via `config_sync`, which runs before any review and so cannot carry a snippet the user has not authored yet; and it does not rely on `folder_sync`, a user-controlled job that can be disabled or filtered — no job's correctness may depend on another job running.
108	
109	### Review, failure and dry-run (D-24 through D-28)
110	
111	Each job's batched review, grouped by action, precedes any change that job makes. Conflicts and version mismatches are diff classes inside that review, not a second reporting mechanism. Non-interactive runs skip all once and record nothing. A failing item does not stop the job — continue, collect, report, and the job result is a failure. The target always downloads from its own repos; no source-cache reuse.
112	
113	### folder_sync overlap (D-29)
114	
115	Package jobs export their owned paths to `folder_sync` via the ADR-018 mechanism, which turns them into non-overridable filters without knowing anything about either ecosystem: `flatpak_sync` owns `~/.local/share/flatpak`, and `snap_sync` owns the retained OLDER `~/snap/<app>/<rev>` revision dirs only. The CURRENT revision's dir is deliberately NOT excluded — `folder_sync` mirrors it, so the active revision's per-user app data travels, which is the whole point of converging the revision (D-06). Older revision dirs are excluded to avoid planting data for revisions the target's snapd never installed, and when the active revision cannot be determined all of that app's revision dirs are excluded as the safe default.
116	
117	## Consequences
118	
119	**Positive:**
120	- Package managers stay authoritative for their own dependency resolution and state, avoiding the correctness problems of file-level package database replication.
121	- Keeping each job's review inside its own `execute()` keeps four independent jobs independent — separate enable flags, config, validation, failure isolation and progress — with no shared ordering surface that could couple one job's failure to another's.
122	- Determining the real transaction at plan time catches collateral dependency changes before anything is applied, so a legitimate install is not blocked by a dependency nobody chose.
123	
124	**Negative (costly to reverse):**
125	- The manifest schema, the item identity scheme and the decision-file format are all shaped by D-01; switching to file-level replication later would replace the whole job core.
126	- The decision files' location under `~/.config/pc-switcher/` means moving them later requires migrating user state on every machine.
127	- Package sync requires passwordless sudo on BOTH machines: the source's `/etc/apt` state and snap configuration are root-only reads.
128	
129	## Alternatives Considered
130	
131	- **File-level replication of the package databases** (`/var/lib/dpkg`, `/var/lib/snapd`, the flatpak OSTree store) — rejected: the package managers must stay authoritative for their own state, and file-level replication would fight their own consistency mechanisms.
132	- **A single combined `package_sync` job** — rejected per D-15: four separate jobs give independent enable flags, independent config, independent failure isolation and independent progress reporting, at the cost of one shared core module holding only what all four use.

gh:

```
code:
  Installed: 1.129.1-1784303641

```

  Installed: 23.01+dfsg-11ubuntu0.1~esm1

  Installed: (none)
  Candidate: (none)
  Version table:
```

```
docker.io:

  Candidate: (none)
  Version table:

        510 https://esm.ubuntu.com/apps/ubuntu noble-apps-security/main amd64 Packages
        500 http://ftp.belnet.be/ubuntu noble-updates/universe amd64 Packages

        100 /var/lib/dpkg/status

Ran the **shipped** `_installed_origins_by_package` (`apt_sync.py:737`) and `_packages_with_no_candidate` (`apt_sync.py:597`) against `apt-cache policy $(apt-mark showmanual)` on this machine:

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| `apt-mark showmanual` names | 153 |
| `_packages_with_no_candidate(...)` | `{'docker.io'}` |
| names with **no repo origin on the installed version** | `{'brother-udev-rule-type1', 'brscan3', 'cnpg', 'code', 'falco-app'}` |
| names with ≥1 repo origin | 148 (148 + 5 = 153 — every name produced a block) |

The 148+5=153 identity also proves the source-side inference is sound: **every installed package yields a block**, so on a `showmanual`-derived name list, "absent from `_installed_origins_by_package`'s dict" ⟺ "installed version's only origin is `/var/lib/dpkg/status`".

## 2. Call sites

### Site A — `apt_sync.collect_unavailable_item_ids` (`apt_sync.py:1223`, policy call at `:1234`)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Machine queried | **TARGET** (`self.target.run_command`, `apt_sync.py:1233`) |
| Input set | `missing_item_ids` — computed at `apt_sync.py:1268-1270` (and again at `:1999-2001`) as *source `apt-mark showmanual` items* minus *target `apt-mark showmanual` items*, both after `filter_inert` |
| Necessarily installed on the queried machine? | **No — and not even necessarily absent.** "Missing" means *absent from the target's manual set*, not *not installed*. An auto-installed-but-not-manual target package reaches this call site. |
| Question actually asked | "Can the target's apt install this package right now?" |
| Literal test verdict | **Correct but incomplete.** |

Reachability of the auto-installed case is not theoretical: the integration suite manufactures it deliberately (`tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py:271-275`, "a selection-state flip changes what `apt_sync` captures without changing what is on the disk", via `apt-mark manual`/`apt-mark auto`).

Why *correct*: `Candidate: (none)` means apt will refuse to install — true for the virtual case (1f) and for the negative-pin case (`docker.io`, 1f), and both correctly become `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY` at `apt_sync.py:363-374`.

Why *incomplete*: the dominant real case — a hand-`.deb` name the target's apt has never heard of — prints **nothing** (1c), so it falls through to `MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`INSTALL` and fails at apply with `Unable to locate package`. That fall-through is **deliberate and asserted**: `tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py:1888-1907` documents "absence must read as 'no evidence against'" because this run may be about to add the repo that provides it.

Why the origin-based predicate must **not** be used here: for the auto-installed-from-a-bare-`.deb` target package (`Candidate: <ver>`, dpkg-status origin only), `apt-get install <name>` succeeds — it just flips the package to manual. The origin test would wrongly declare it `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` and suppress a correct, cheap action.

### Site B — `manual_installs_sync._scan_no_candidate_apt_packages` (`manual_installs_sync.py:391`, policy call at `:401`)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Machine queried | **SOURCE** (`self.source.run_command`, `manual_installs_sync.py:401`) |
| Input set | `manual_names` = the source's own `apt-mark showmanual` (`manual_installs_sync.py:443-447`) |
| Necessarily installed on the queried machine? | **Yes.** Verified: all 153 `showmanual` names on this machine are `ii`, and each produced a policy block. |
| Question actually asked | "Was this installed from a bare `.deb`, i.e. can no configured repository reproduce it?" (module docstring `manual_installs_sync.py:6-8`; ADR-020 D-18) |
| Literal test verdict | **Wrong.** Measured: 1 false positive (`docker.io`), 5 false negatives (§1g). |

`_packages_with_no_candidate`'s copy at `manual_installs_sync.py:142-163` is byte-identical to `apt_sync.py:597-615`; its docstring at `:145-148` explicitly justifies the duplication.

## 3. Fix proposal

### 3.1 Correct predicates

They differ. Two predicates, one parse.

**Site B (source, `manual_installs_sync`) — replace entirely.**

New rule: a name from the source's `apt-mark showmanual` is `apt-no-candidate` iff its **installed** version has no repository origin, i.e. every origin row under its `***` version is `/var/lib/dpkg/status`. Nothing else — not `Candidate: (none)`, not block absence.

Signature to add to the shared module (§3.2):

```
def packages_installed_from_no_repository(
    policy_output: str, queried_names: Sequence[str]
) -> frozenset[str]
```

- `queried_names` is required because the origins map omits a package entirely when it has no repo origin (`apt_sync.py:753`, `origins.setdefault` is only reached inside the `parts[1] != "/var/lib/dpkg/status"` guard) — "no origins" is representable only as absence, and absence needs the queried list to be distinguished from "never asked".
- Returns `{name for name in queried_names if not origins.get(name)}`, where `origins` is `installed_origins_by_package(policy_output)`.
- Docstring must state the precondition: **callers must pass only names known to be installed** (a not-installed name would be indistinguishable from a dpkg-only one). At the only call site that precondition holds by construction — the list is `apt-mark showmanual`.
- Deliberate consequence to document: a package hand-installed at version 2.0 while a repo offers 1.0 **is** flagged unreproducible. That is correct under D-18 — replicating *this machine's* installed version needs the `.deb`, not the repo's older one.

Call site change at `manual_installs_sync.py:402`: swap `_packages_with_no_candidate(result.stdout)` for `packages_installed_from_no_repository(result.stdout, manual_names)`. Nothing else in that function moves; the label at `:404` (`f"{name} (no apt candidate)"`) should be reworded to say what is now actually meant — e.g. name that no configured repository provides it — since "no apt candidate" is now literally false for every item it produces.

**Site A (target, `apt_sync`) — keep the predicate, decide separately about the blind spot.**

Keep `Candidate: (none)` as-is at `apt_sync.py:1234`. It answers Site A's question correctly.

The remaining gap (empty block ⇒ silently offered ⇒ `Unable to locate package` at apply) is a **separate open decision, not part of this fix**. Presenting the options rather than picking:

- **(i) Leave it.** Deliberate today, locked in by `tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py:1888`. Cost: every hand-`.deb` package on the source is proposed as an apt install that is *guaranteed* to fail, once per sync, forever — because the source-side fix in Site B does *not* suppress apt_sync's own diff (D-15 forbids the cross-job coupling that would; this is exactly the undecided matrix-A11 double-surfacing in handover §4).
- **(ii) Strict only in the second pass.** Make `_replanned_package_diffs` (`apt_sync.py:1991`) treat an empty block as unavailable, since after `apt-get update` no further repo work is coming. Cheap, but the second pass only runs when repository work was approved (`apt_sync.py:1885-1887`), so a run with no `/etc/apt` changes is unfixed.
- **(iii) Ask the source instead.** Have `apt_sync.capture_source_items` (`apt_sync.py:1126`) run one extra batched `apt-cache policy` on the **source** over the same `showmanual` list and reuse `packages_installed_from_no_repository`. A package that came from no repo *on the source* cannot come from a repo on the target either, independent of target repo state and of ordering — so it classifies deterministically at plan time, with no second-pass dependency and no cross-job coupling. Costs one read command on the source, and needs its own detail wording (`build_repo_unavailable_detail`, `apt_sync.py:267-272`, currently says "target's repositories offer no candidate", which would be the wrong sentence). Also requires a new entry in `_READ_ONLY_CALLS` (`tests/unit/test_mutates_audit.py:116` currently pins `capture_source_items` at 1 `run_command`).

Recommendation: **(iii)**, with (i) as the do-nothing fallback. It is the only option that fixes the case the handover actually observed (`code` proposed as an install that fails) without depending on whether the run happens to touch `/etc/apt`.

### 3.2 Where the shared parser lives

**New module: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/apt_policy.py`.** Move `_installed_origins_by_package` (`apt_sync.py:737-775`), `_normalise_repo_uri` (`apt_sync.py:684-690`, its only dependency), and `_packages_with_no_candidate` (`apt_sync.py:597-615`) there as public functions; add `packages_installed_from_no_repository` alongside. Delete both `_packages_with_no_candidate` copies from `apt_sync.py` and `manual_installs_sync.py:142-163`.

Justification against **D-15** (`docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md:79`, "one manager's diff on the shared base would make the other three inherit inputs they never supply"):

- D-15's stated harm is **inheritance**, on the shared *base class*. `apt_policy.py` defines no class and is not in `PackageSyncJob`'s MRO. `snap_sync` and `flatpak_sync` simply never import it and inherit nothing new. The `packages/` package is not exclusively `PackageSyncJob` — `state.py` and `review.py` are already free-function/standalone-class modules imported selectively.
- It also satisfies **D-18**'s actual constraint (`manual_installs_sync.py:17-18`, "never imports `apt_sync`") — the dependency runs `manual_installs_sync → apt_policy ← apt_sync`, with neither job importing the other. Today's alternative is what D-18 chose: duplication, justified at `manual_installs_sync.py:94-96` as "one duplicated line is cheaper than a shared-core coupling". That premise no longer holds — the correct parser is a ~25-line stateful indentation walker with three subtle rules (`***` marker, exact 8-space origin indent, dpkg-status skip), not one line. `apt_sync.py:778-786` documents the project's own precedent for what duplicating a parser of this size costs: `_pin_packages`/`_parse_pin_file` diverged and silently lost every name after the first.

If the user prefers to keep D-18's zero-shared-code rule literally, the fallback is to duplicate the *origin* parser into `manual_installs_sync` too — but then the report should note that the project now maintains two copies of a 25-line parser, and 3.1's shared-signature guidance applies per copy.

### 3.3 Should `_packages_with_no_candidate` be deleted?

**Retain, do not delete.** Move it to `apt_policy.py` and export it as `packages_with_no_candidate`; its single remaining caller is `apt_sync.collect_unavailable_item_ids` (`apt_sync.py:1234`), where it is correct. Delete only the `manual_installs_sync.py:142-163` copy.

Its docstring must be corrected on the move: the current one at `apt_sync.py:598-601` implies `(none)` is what apt prints for an uninstallable package, which §1c disproves. It should say: `(none)` means apt knows the name but will not install it (pure virtual, or every version pinned below zero — `docker.io` is the observed case); a name apt has never heard of produces **no block at all** and is therefore absent from the result, which the caller reads as "no evidence against".

### 3.4 Consequences

**`manual_installs_sync` detection flow (`manual_installs_sync.py:402` area).** No structural change: `_scan_no_candidate_apt_packages` keeps its shape (one batched policy read on the source, `manual_installs_sync.py:400-406`), `capture_source_items` (`:434-448`) keeps passing `manual_names` (now used for both the command and the predicate), and everything downstream — `filter_inert`, `plan()`'s snippet lookup at `:474-494`, the carved `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` group at `:497-526` — is unchanged. What changes is *which* items appear: on the user's P17, one wrong item (`docker.io`) disappears and five real ones (`brother-udev-rule-type1`, `brscan3`, `cnpg`, `code`, `falco-app`) appear. **D-18's calibration in the handover ("4 apt packages have no repo candidate") is superseded: the measured number is 5.**

Also `tests/unit/test_mutates_audit.py:152` pins `_scan_no_candidate_apt_packages` at 1 `run_command` — unchanged by this fix (still exactly one policy read).

**The second review (commit `089ea985`).** The handover's line reference is wrong: `_rereview_repo_invalidated_packages` is at **`apt_sync.py:1899-1989`**, not 1410-1441 (that range is inside `_diff_apt_sources`/the orphaned-packages detail). Its gate is `apt_sync.py:1885-1887`. Consequences:

- With Site A's predicate unchanged, the second review is **unaffected** by this fix. It calls `collect_unavailable_item_ids` through `_replanned_package_diffs` (`apt_sync.py:2002`) with the same semantics as the first pass, so a `(none)` → available transition after `apt-get update` still reaches the user the same run, exactly as the handover describes.
- If option (ii) or (iii) from §3.1 is adopted, the second pass changes meaning and needs its own test: under (iii), the *source-side* origin fact does not change after `apt-get update`, so a package classified unavailable-by-source-origin must **stay** unavailable across the re-diff rather than flipping to `INSTALL` and being re-offered. That is the one new invariant (iii) introduces.
- `manual_installs_sync` has no second review and is unaffected either way.

### 4.1 Existing tests that pass because of the wrong predicate

All in `tests/unit/jobs/test_manual_installs_sync.py`. Every one feeds a `Candidate: (none)` policy fixture that, under the corrected predicate, yields **no** unreproducible item — so every one of these currently passes for the wrong reason and goes RED on the fix until its fixture is replaced with the §1a shape.

| 170-172 | `test_no_candidate_source_package_becomes_unreproducible_diff` (166) |
| 232 | `test_item_with_snippet_plans_install_and_converges_by_replaying_it` (228) |
| 261 | `test_item_without_snippet_is_report_only_and_grouped_separately` (257) |

| 431 | `test_plan_runs_with_apt_absent_from_config_and_manual_enabled` (427) |

| 476 | `test_detect_plan_and_replay_end_to_end` (472) |
| 540 | `test_on_the_fly_snippet_is_replayed_the_same_run` (517) |

The exception is `test_no_candidate_source_package_becomes_unreproducible_diff` (166), which is the detection test itself and should be replaced by the new tests in 4.2.

**Not affected, verified:** `tests/unit/jobs/test_package_sync_core.py` never parses policy output — its `apt-no-candidate` references (lines 447, 465, 480, 500, 526, 536) are hardcoded item-id strings only. `tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py` `TestUnavailableCapture` (990-1042), `test_a_package_apt_reports_no_candidate_for_is_withheld_from_the_first_pass` (1868) and `test_a_package_apt_has_never_heard_of_prints_no_block_and_is_still_offered` (1888) all stay green under §3.1's Site A decision (keep the predicate) — and under option (iii) only `:1888` would need revisiting.

### 4.2 New unit tests

It surfaced a structural finding worth stating before the questions: removing the source item **breaks the feature unless the package diff changes too**. `collect_unavailable_item_ids` asks the *target's* apt for a candidate, so a package needing a repo the target lacks becomes `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY` — not an INSTALL — so it can approve nothing, so the repo is never derived. `_diff_apt_packages` needs a `repo_supplied_item_ids` override to make "install gh (adds repo cli.github.com)" representable at all. That also means those packages can't be `apt-get -s` simulated at plan time (the repo isn't there yet), so their collateral moves to the second review.

Four forks in the design need your ruling:

questions.question: A source file present on BOTH machines with different content (names.changed, apt_sync.py:1561-1584) is neither an add nor a removal. Your decision doesn't cover it. What happens to it?

options.label: Stays a reviewed CHANGE item (Recommended)
options.description: Smallest change, and the only option that keeps a content change visible. No package install can fail for want of it (the repo already exists on the target), so it needs no derivation. Keeps _travelling_keyrings_detail and the changed-source dangling-key downgrade alive, and keeps apt:source: skip-always meaningful in the source-held direction. Cost: one APT_SOURCE item is still tickable, so the review isn't purely add-derived/remove-reviewed.

options.label: Also derived
options.description: A package from that repo drags the newer file over. Simplest mental model: you never decide about a repo you are adding OR updating. But a changed file can NARROW a repo (drop a component, change a suite, move a URI), which is closer to destructive than additive — and it would land with no decision.

options.label: Dropped entirely
options.description: Repos never converge their content once present on the target. Cheapest to build, and arguably matches the rationale (you only add a repo because you want a package). But it silently freezes a stale target repo forever — a suite bump or URI move on the source never propagates, with nothing in the review saying so.

questions.question: "Never collected" is specified as ubuntu.sources + /etc/apt/sources.list. Measured on your machine, sources.list.d ALSO holds ubuntu.sources.save, ubuntu.sources.curtin.orig, ubuntu-esm-apps.sources(.save), ubuntu-esm-infra.sources(.save) — all captured and diffed today, since _capture_dir_digests is -type f with no extension filter. How wide should the exclusion be?

options.label: Extension filter + esm + ubuntu.sources (Recommended)
options.description: Collect only *.list and *.sources (kills .save/.curtin.orig outright — apt ignores them, and curtin.orig names archive.ubuntu.com while your ubuntu.sources names a local mirror, so syncing it would push a machine-specific mirror choice). Plus never-collect ubuntu.sources and ubuntu-esm-*.sources: 7 of your manual packages resolve to esm.ubuntu.com, and those files are managed by ubuntu-advantage-tools and tied to a per-machine Pro attachment — deriving an add would copy a Pro repo to an unattached machine.

options.label: Extension filter + ubuntu.sources only
options.description: Collect only *.list and *.sources, and never-collect ubuntu.sources. Leaves the ubuntu-esm-*.sources files syncable — accepting that a Pro repo may be pushed to a machine with no Pro attachment, where apt-get update will complain.

options.label: Exactly as specified, nothing more
options.description: Never-collect ubuntu.sources and /etc/apt/sources.list by exact filename; leave everything else as today. The .save and .curtin.orig backup files keep being diffed and offered, and the esm files keep syncing.

questions.question: If you previously declined a repo addition, apt:source:foo.sources sits in ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml on the SOURCE machine. After this change nothing reads that entry — so the repo gets derived anyway, silently overriding your earlier "never sync this".

options.label: Honour them — skip derivation (Recommended)
options.description: _derived_sources_for_package consults the already-loaded source decision file and drops any file recorded there. Costs one set lookup. Consequence: a repo can then be permanently blocked with no way to unblock it from the review — only by hand-editing apt.decisions.yaml, since there's no longer an item to re-decide.

options.label: Ignore them — derive anyway
options.description: Add-direction entries become inert data. A repo you once declined comes back the moment you approve a package from it — which is arguably correct under the new model (you approved the package, the repo follows), but it silently reverses an explicit past decision with no notice.

options.label: Ignore, but say so in the detail
options.description: Derive the repo anyway, and have the package's review detail note that a prior decline is being overridden. Keeps the new model coherent while making the reversal visible. Costs extra detail wording and a lookup.

questions.question: How should the repository be named on the package's review line? Your example used the URI host ("adds repo cli.github.com"), but 43a52fa3's removal detail uses the FILENAME, and filename is the item identity everywhere else in the codebase.

options.label: Host for adds, filename for removals (Recommended)
options.description: Matches your example and reads better — cli.github.com is the token you recognise, github-cli.list is not. Inconsistent with the removal direction, but the two directions are now genuinely different kinds of thing: an add is derived and identified by where packages come from, a removal is a reviewed item identified by the file being deleted.

options.label: Both, host then filename
options.description: e.g. names the host and the file it writes. Fully unambiguous and consistent, at the cost of a longer review line — and the review is already dense.

content.text:
Task 1 is **done and green**. Four commits, none pushed. One thing worth flagging: the design I briefed had a real defect, which the agent caught and fixed rather than shipping — `packages_installed_from_no_repository` treated *"apt printed nothing"* as *"no repository supplies this"*. A failed or empty `apt-cache policy` would have declared a machine's entire 153-package manual set unreproducible, and once wired into `apt_sync`'s capture it would have dropped the whole manifest and synced nothing, silently. `installed_origins_by_package` now records a key per block header, so "apt says no repo supplies this" is representable apart from "apt said nothing". Fixed in `df48cd07`, ahead of the exclusion in `30a9eb6f`. All four mutations went RED; none failed to fail.

On your question about collateral — it's D-30, and it isn't "install or skip". `apt-get --dry-run install X` may reveal that satisfying X requires **removing or downgrading some other package** the user manually installed. That third package never appears in any diff; it's not being synced. So the question is "installing X will remove Y — install anyway, skip X, or abort?" For a repo-supplied package we can't simulate at plan time (the repo isn't on the target yet), so that specific question can only be asked after `/etc/apt` converges. That's all I meant.

Your Firefox case is a serious finding and it's bigger than the derived-repos work. `collect_unavailable_item_ids` matches on **name only**. Source Firefox from Mozilla + pin, target has Ubuntu's Firefox available → target reports a candidate → apt_sync proposes an ordinary install → **the target silently installs a different package from a different vendor**. That is a wrong-package bug that exists today, independent of derived repos, and it also means the whole "ask the target's apt at plan time" model is unsound while `/etc/apt` is still diverged.

Three things need your ruling before I can brief the implementation:

questions.question: The Firefox danger: apt_sync matches packages by NAME only, so a package the source gets from a vendor repo can be silently installed from Ubuntu's archive on the target. How should the plan establish that the target will install the SAME thing?

options.label: Match on (name, origin) at plan time (Recommended)
options.description: Stop asking the target "do you have a candidate for X" and start asking "do you have a candidate for X from the origin the source installed it from". Both halves are already computable at plan time: the source's origin URI per package via installed_origins_by_package, and which repos this run will add via the derivation. A target candidate from a DIFFERENT origin is a mismatch, not an install. Keeps one review, and kills the repo-availability half of the second review entirely.

options.label: Converge all of /etc/apt first, then diff packages once
options.description: Sync every source repo and pin to the target before computing the package diff at all, so the target's apt is authoritative when asked. Simplest and safest logic, and no second review needed. But it abandons derived repos — repos would be synced wholesale rather than derived from approved packages, which reverses the decision in section 2 of the handover.

options.label: Name match now, verify origin before install
options.description: Keep the plan-time diff as it is, and re-check each approved package's origin after /etc/apt converges, refusing any install whose origin does not match the source's. Smallest change to the current shape. But the user has already approved "install firefox" on a screen that showed the wrong provenance, and the refusal arrives mid-apply.

questions.question: You wrote "There is no 'reviewed item': we only review packages." That contradicts the handover, which says repo REMOVAL stays reviewed because it is destructive and affects packages that remain. Which holds?

options.label: Removal stays its own reviewed item
options.description: As the handover specifies. Deleting a repo on the target gets its own tickable line, unticked by default, naming what it would strand (43a52fa3's orphaned-packages detail). Packages are reviewed AND repo removals are reviewed — the add direction is the only derived one.

options.label: Only packages are ever reviewed
options.description: Taking your sentence literally: repo removal is also derived — a repo disappears when the last package needing it is removed, with no line of its own. Consistent and simpler, but it makes a destructive /etc/apt change with no explicit decision, and reference counting becomes load-bearing on a delete — which the handover specifically said it must not be.

options.label: Removal derived, but named on the package line
options.description: The repo goes when its last package goes, and the package's removal line says so ("remove gh (also deletes repo cli.github.com)"). Nothing is tickable except packages, but the destructive system change is still disclosed before you approve it.

questions.question: apt_sync now drops bare-.deb packages at capture and leaves them to manual_installs_sync (your A11 ruling, shipped). Since apt_sync may not read another job's enable flag (D-15), disabling manual_installs_sync while apt_sync stays on means those 5 packages (code, brscan3, cnpg, falco-app, brother-udev-rule-type1) are replicated by nobody — silently.

options.label: Document it and move on (Recommended)
options.description: Already done — apt_sync's module docstring and both package-sync docs carry the warning. Disabling a job and losing what it owned is the expected meaning of an enable flag, and the four-jobs-are-independent rule (D-15/D-16) is worth more than this edge.

options.label: Warn at validate() time
options.description: If apt_sync is enabled and manual_installs_sync is not, emit a warning naming the packages that will go unreplicated. Fits your "validate env assumptions early, with copy-paste remediation" rule. Costs one config read — arguably a lighter coupling than a job reading another's runtime state, but it is still apt_sync knowing manual_installs_sync exists.

options.label: Report them as REPORT_ONLY in apt_sync
options.description: apt_sync keeps surfacing them as unactionable report lines so they are never invisible, regardless of which jobs are on. Costs the double-surfacing you just ruled against — both jobs would name the same 5 packages when both are enabled.

All gates green after the sweep: **1289 passed**, pyright 0, ruff clean. ~700 flag expansions across 12 tools, each verified against the man page on Ubuntu 24.04 (same release as the targets). The agent correctly left alone flags with no long form (`ssh` has none at all; `kill -9` runs through bash's builtin, not util-linux) and refused to expand `xargs -I`, whose `--replace=` alias is documented as deprecated. It also flagged that `README.md` and `install.sh` now drift — I'll pick those up separately since they're user-facing.

Your three answers plus the two earlier ones now fully specify task 2. My reading, before I brief it:

- **Review lists packages only.** Each shows its origin when that isn't Ubuntu. Decision is apply/skip. `apt_sync` then does whatever is necessary — repo, key, pin — to install from *that same origin*, or to remove from the target.
- **Follow-up confirmation only** when the operation would impact machine-specific packages on the target.
- **Repo removal** is reviewed, but two-way only: remove or skip-once. No decision-file entry.
- **Repo content change**: overwrite the target silently, *unless* a machine-specific package on the target comes from that repo — then show both versions and ask overwrite or skip-once.
- **`ubuntu.sources` / esm files**: never removed, but updated, and added if missing. Warn with remediation if an ESM repo lands on a machine with no Pro attachment.
- **No backwards compatibility** anywhere — no `apt:source:` decision records exist.

One assumption I'm carrying: **packages keep the three-way decision and the machine-local registry** (ADR-020 D-07/D-08, already built). You said "no registry, YAGNI" specifically about repo removals, and contrasted it with packages — tell me if you meant it for packages too.

DESIGN/SPEC task in /home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher, branch `gsd/phase-02-package-management-sync`. Write ONE spec document. DO NOT change any source file, do NOT commit, do NOT push. Do not touch the pc1/pc2 VMs or the Hetzner lock. Read-only shell commands only (`git show`, `grep`, `apt-cache policy`, `apt-mark showmanual`) — nothing that changes this machine.

## Why this document exists

The user has just made a series of rulings that simplify the apt review model well below what the current code implements, and that also fix a live wrong-package bug. A previous design pass produced a plan for "derived repos" that is now partly superseded. Your job is to write the single reconciled spec that implementation will be briefed from.

## Read first

- `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-HANDOVER-package-review.md`
- `docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md` — especially D-02, D-07, D-08, D-11, D-12, D-13, D-24, D-30
- `docs/adr/adr-001-adr.md` — the ADR process, including immutability after acceptance

- `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-SCENARIO-COVERAGE.md`

## The rulings — these are decided, do not re-litigate or re-open them

1. **The review lists packages, and only packages.** Each line shows the package and, when its origin is not the Ubuntu archive, that origin. The user chooses apply or skip. `apt_sync` then does whatever is necessary — add the repository, carry its signing key, write the pin — so the target installs **from the same origin the source installed from**, or removes it from the target.

2. **Origin is part of what gets replicated.** This fixes a live bug: `collect_unavailable_item_ids` (`apt_sync.py:1157`) matches on NAME only, so a source machine running Firefox from the Mozilla repo under a pin, syncing to a target where Ubuntu's archive also offers `firefox`, gets a target candidate, an ordinary INSTALL, and **silently installs a different vendor's package**. The user's words: "Target will say it can install Firefox, even without having the mozilla repo, so target would install from ubuntu repo. DANGER."

3. **A follow-up confirmation is asked in exactly one situation**: when the operation would impact **machine-specific packages on the target** (i.e. packages recorded skip-always in the target's decision file). Not otherwise.

4. **Repository ADD is derived** from the packages approved from it — never a tickable line of its own. This makes "package ticked, its source unticked" unrepresentable.

5. **Repository REMOVAL is reviewed, two-way only: remove or skip-once.** The user's words: "Reviewed: ok, but only remove/skip-once. No registry. YAGNI." So a repo removal gets a review line, but there is NO skip-always and NO machine-local decision-file entry for it.

6. **Repository CHANGE (same file, both machines, different content)**: overwrite the target silently in the normal case. The ONE exception: if a machine-specific package on the target comes from the repo that changed, show the two versions (the user's words: "diff is not very readable" — so show the versions, not a unified diff) and ask overwrite or skip-once. Skip-once only: the user's words, "user has effectively only the choice to delay until next sync: user should consolidate themselves."

7. **`ubuntu.sources`, `/etc/apt/sources.list` and the `ubuntu-esm-*` files are never REMOVED, but they are updated, and added to the target if missing.** The user pushed back on the word "collect": "Do not remove them. But update them. And if not present on target (possibly esm), add them. Issue warning if ESM added but machine not attached to Pro, with instructions. User wants to sync machines. User selects apt-sync. So user wants package sources to be the same on both." Note this REVISES the handover's "never collected" line, whose actual concern was deletion — say so explicitly in the doc so the two don't read as a contradiction.

8. **No backwards compatibility, anywhere.** The user's words: "There are no old decisions. We are still in development. Package-sync has never run anywhere but in test-environment. Don't do backwards compatibility anywhere! There are no apt:source decision records at all!" No migration code, no reading of legacy entries, no compatibility shims.

9. **The repository is named by its full URI path**, not just the host and not the filename. The user's words: "Always host (the full path: `ppa.launchpadcontent.net/git-core/ppa/ubuntu/` instead of `ppa.launchpadcontent.net` which doesn't tell anything)."

10. **Bare-`.deb` packages are `manual_installs_sync`'s exclusive territory** — already shipped in `30a9eb6f`. "Each of the 4 has a clear scope. No overlap."

11. **Long CLI options everywhere** — already swept in `ab570e93`. Any command you specify must use long forms.

## Assumption to state and flag, not to silently resolve

Ruling 5 says "no registry" about repo removals. I am carrying the assumption that **packages keep their three-way decision and their machine-local registry** (ADR-020 D-07/D-08, already implemented) — the user contrasted repos against packages rather than abolishing the registry outright. State this assumption prominently near the top of the doc as an open confirmation, and design as if it holds.

## Deliverable

Write `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-SPEC-package-review-model.md`. It must be implementation-ready: a fresh agent should be able to build from it without asking clarifying questions. Sections:

### 1. The model in one page
The review's complete shape after these rulings: what appears, what is derived, what is asked, what is never asked. A reader should be able to picture the screens.

### 2. Origin replication
How "install from the same origin" is established and enforced. The source's origin URIs per package come from `installed_origins_by_package` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/apt_policy.py`); each source file's URIs from `_parse_source_file` (`apt_sync.py`). Specify the mapping and every case that breaks it: package served by several repos; origin matching no source file; target candidate from a DIFFERENT origin than the source's (the Firefox case — what happens, exactly); target candidate from the SAME origin (no repo work needed); no target candidate at all. Say precisely what replaces the current `collect_unavailable_item_ids` question, and whether pins must travel for the origin to actually win on the target (Firefox needs the Mozilla pin, or apt may still prefer Ubuntu's — verify this against how apt priorities work and say so).

### 3. Ordering and the transaction
Where derivation runs (plan vs converge), how the `/etc/apt` group stays transactional (ADR-020's boundary), the key -> source -> pin -> `apt-get update` -> package ordering, and what happens to the second mid-`execute()` review from `089ea985`. State plainly whether that second review still has a reason to exist under this model, and if it does, what remains in it. If it can go, say what deleting it simplifies.

### 4. The machine-specific follow-up (ruling 3)
Exact trigger condition, what is shown, what is asked, what each answer does. Cover both the repo-change case (ruling 6) and the D-30 collateral case, and say whether these are one mechanism or two.

### 5. Never-removed source files (ruling 7)
Which filenames, matched how. The ESM/Pro warning: trigger condition, wording constraints, and the remediation the user must be given. Note the user's rule that environment assumptions are validated early with copy-paste remediation, never mid-execute — decide whether the Pro check belongs in `validate()` and justify it.

### 6. What gets deleted
Every function, item class, review group, test and doc paragraph that this model makes dead. Be specific with `path:line`. Include what disappears from `packages/items.py`, `sync_core.py`'s verb table, and the `APT_SOURCE` add-direction machinery.

### 7. Blast radius
Existing tests that must change or die, by `path:line`. Rows of `02-SCENARIO-COVERAGE.md` invalidated, by row id. Docs to update (`docs/jobs/package-sync.md`, `docs/system/package-sync.md`, module docstrings).

### 8. ADR
`docs/adr/adr-001-adr.md:15` makes accepted ADRs immutable — they are superseded, not edited. ADR-020 is `Status: Accepted`. Specify the superseding ADR: its number (check `docs/adr/_index.md` for the next free one), title, which ADR-020 decisions it overturns and which it carries forward unchanged. ### 9. Staged implementation plan
Break the work into stages that each end green (gates pass, tests meaningful), in dependency order, with what each stage delivers. Small enough that a single agent can do one stage. Say which stages can run in parallel without touching the same regions of `apt_sync.py`.

### 10. Test plan
Per behaviour: exact test name, what it asserts, and the mutation that proves it can go RED (what to break, what should then fail). Tests create the environment they need — no discover-or-skip, no `pytest.skip` in `tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py`; VM fixtures live in `tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh`. The Firefox scenario specifically needs a test: two repos offering the same package name, and the target must not install the wrong one.

Only genuine ones — where two readings of the rulings above lead to materially different code. Do not pad this; the user has answered a lot already and re-asking answered questions wastes their time.

Per CLAUDE.md: prose specs, exact function signatures, parameter names, behaviour rules — **NOT ready-made implementations**. Do NOT paste existing source into the doc; reference by `path:line`. """

import asyncio

from rich.console import Console

from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.review import (
    COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION,
    UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION,
    ReviewEntry,
    ReviewGroup,
    review_items,
)
from pcswitcher.ui import TerminalUI

# One group per interaction kind the review supports. The action strings are load-bearing:
# "install" is checked by default, "remove" is not (_REMOVAL_ACTIONS, review.py:100), and
# "report" sits outside _ACTIONABLE_ACTIONS (review.py:108) so its group must be offered
# NO never-offer-again screen.
GROUPS = [
    ReviewGroup(
        "apt",
        "install",
        "Install apt packages",
        [
            ReviewEntry("apt:package:sl", "sl 5.02-2", "install"),
            ReviewEntry("apt:package:cowsay", "cowsay 3.03+dfsg2-8", "install"),
            # Brackets in untrusted text: Rich would parse these as markup if the label
            # were not wrapped in Text. A crash here is the bug this entry exists to catch.
            ReviewEntry("apt:package:weird", "weird [bold red]name[/] 1.0", "install"),
        ],
    ),
    ReviewGroup(
        "apt",
        "remove",
        "Remove apt packages",
        [
            ReviewEntry("apt:package:libfoo1", "libfoo1 1.2-3", "remove"),
            ReviewEntry(
                "apt:package:oldpkg",
                "oldpkg 0.9",
                "remove",
                "removal leaves 3 packages without updates",
            ),
        ],
    ),
    ReviewGroup(
        "apt",
        "report",
        "apt version mismatches (report only)",
        [
            ReviewEntry("apt:package:vim", "vim: source 9.1 / target 9.0", "report"),
        ],
    ),
    ReviewGroup(
        "apt",
        COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION,
        "Manually-installed collateral",
        [
            ReviewEntry(
                "apt:collateral:file",
                "file",
                "review",
                "would be removed by removing the selected packages",
            ),
        ],
    ),
    ReviewGroup(
        "manual_installs",
        UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION,
        "Resolve manual_installs items with no reproducible install",
        [
            ReviewEntry("unreproducible:unowned-path:/opt/pcsw-uat-app", "/opt/pcsw-uat-app", "resolve"),
        ],
    ),
]


async def main() -> None:
    console = Console()
    ui = TerminalUI(console=console, total_steps=1)
    ui.start()
    try:
        outcome = await review_items(GROUPS, console=console, ui=ui)
    finally:
        ui.stop()

    console.rule("decisions")
    for item_id, decision in sorted(outcome.decisions.items()):
        console.print(f"  {item_id}: {decision}")
    console.rule("snippets")
    for item_id, snippet in sorted(outcome.snippets.items()):
        console.print(f"  {item_id}:\n{snippet}")
    console.rule("unresolved")
    console.print(f"  {outcome.unresolved}")
    console.print(f"\nwas_interactive={outcome.was_interactive}")


asyncio.run(main())

## Running the review harness

The file is at:

```

It touches nothing — no machine contacted, no file written, no package manager invoked. It renders the real prompts against the real `TerminalUI` and prints the decisions it collected.

### What you'll be asked, in order

1. **Install apt packages** — 3 entries, all pre-ticked. One is labelled `weird [bold red]name[/] 1.0`: if that renders as literal text, the `Text` wrapping is holding; if it renders as red bold or crashes, that's the markup bug.
2. **never offer again on this machine?** — appears only if you leave something unticked above. Tick nothing and press Enter; it must accept that as "leave them for next run", not re-ask.
3. **Remove apt packages** — 2 entries, both must arrive **unticked**. One carries a consequence detail.
4. **apt version mismatches (report only)** — must get **no** never-offer-again screen afterwards, whatever you tick.
5. **Manually-installed collateral** — a three-way select: install-anyway / skip / abort.
6. **Resolve manual_installs items** — a three-way select per entry; choose "Add an install snippet" to open the multi-line editor. Finish with **Esc then Enter** (or Alt+Enter). Submit an empty body once — it must print a yellow "cannot be empty" and re-ask, not fall through.

At the end it prints the decisions, any snippet you authored, and `was_interactive`.

### Key handling to check

- **Ctrl-C** at any prompt → whole run aborts with `SyncAbortedByUser`.
- **Ctrl-D** at any prompt → re-asks that prompt.
- **Enter with nothing ticked** on a checkbox → a real answer (skip all), never a re-ask.

## The model, in short

The apt review becomes three screens: **packages** (each line naming its origin when that origin is not the distribution archive, in ruling-9 full-path form), **repository removals** (two answers — remove or skip once, no registry entry), and **repository conflicts** (only when a file differing on both machines feeds a target skip-always package; shows both file contents, overwrite or skip once). Everything else under `/etc/apt` is derived: repository adds from approved packages, keys as today, pins as an always-sync bucket, plus `ubuntu.sources` / `/etc/apt/sources.list` / `ubuntu-esm-*` written-and-updated but never removed.

Origin replication is established by mapping `installed_origins_by_package` on the source (reusing the policy output `capture_source_items` already fetches at `apt_sync.py:1117`) through `_parse_source_file`'s URIs to source files, and is enforced by a batched `apt-cache policy` on the target **after** `apt-get update` and **before** the first install: candidate origins must intersect the source's, or the item fails. That check, not the derivation, is the hard guarantee.

## Findings worth flagging

- **The pin is load-bearing, verified.** Ubuntu's `firefox` is `1:1snap1-0ubuntu5` at priority 500 (read on the dev machine). Epoch 1 outranks every unpinned vendor version, so adding the Mozilla repo alone still installs Ubuntu's package. Pins must travel. That drove pins into an always-sync bucket rather than a per-package derivation — simpler, and it avoids inventing a `Pin: origin` parser.
- **The second review can be deleted entirely.** Its repo-availability case dissolves because classification now reads the *source's* origins, which no run mutates. Its pin case dissolves only if the `HELD_OR_PINNED` echo goes — which I recommend, because that branch (`apt_sync.py:352-355, 366-376`) is also the cause of the open defect at `02-HANDOVER-package-review.md:62` (a pinned target package can never be removed or silenced). Deleting both removes ~200 lines, eight tests, and the untested mid-`execute()` prompt hazard the handover ranks first.
- **`collect_unavailable_item_ids` (`apt_sync.py:1205`) is the live bug** and `packages_with_no_candidate` becomes dead code once it goes.
- **Unrelated correctness find:** `_capture_dir_digests` uses `find -type f` with no extension filter, so `ubuntu.sources.save`, `ubuntu.sources.curtin.orig` and two `ubuntu-esm-*.sources.save` files (all present on the dev machine, none read by apt) are currently captured as items. Specified a `*.list`/`*.sources` filter for `sources.list.d` only — `preferences.d` legitimately holds extensionless files.

## Conflicts I could not fully reconcile

**ESM on an unattached target.** Ruling 7 says add them and warn. `ValidationError` has no severity (`models.py:103`) and every one aborts the run (`orchestrator.py:1019-1025`), so the Pro check cannot live in `validate()` — I put it in read-only `plan()`, which still satisfies the "never mid-execute" rule. But writing ESM sources to an unattached target likely makes `apt-get update` fail, and the `/etc/apt` group is transactional, so it would roll back every other repository change in the run. I specified **withhold-and-warn** against the literal ruling, and labelled the 401/exit-code premise as an unverified hypothesis. This is open question 5.

**Ruling 3's "exactly one situation" versus D-30.** D-30's collateral prompt triggers on the union of both machines' manual sets (`apt_sync.py:1628`), which is far wider than the skip-always set ruling 3 names. I left D-30 untouched and specified three mechanisms (removal disclosure, conflict prompt, collateral prompt) sharing one machine-specific-by-origin helper. Open question 4.

## Open questions (§11)

1. Packages keep their three-way decision and machine-local registry (stated as an assumption at the top of the doc; ruling 3 presupposes it).
2. `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` — no package derives it; I put it in the always-sync bucket. Alternative readings: review both directions, or drop from scope.
3. Removal of pins and apt config — I gave them the repo-removal two-answer shape by analogy; ruling 5 names repositories only.
4. D-30's collateral trigger versus ruling 3.
5. ESM withhold versus write.

content.text:
Fair challenge — let me correct the framing, because "impacted" was my word and it's misleading.

No apt command ever runs on the source. The source's `apt-mark showmanual` set is already captured as the manifest; D-30 consults it purely as **evidence of your intent**, not as a machine to act on.

The case it covers: apt on the *target* decides it must remove package `Y` to satisfy an approved install. On the target, `Y` is merely an auto-installed dependency — so by the target's own records nobody chose it, and removing it looks harmless. But on the source, `Y` is in `showmanual`: you deliberately installed it there. Since the source is what's being replicated, silently deleting `Y` from the target destroys a package you chose to have — it just happens to have arrived on the target as a dependency rather than by hand. ADR-020 puts it as "the package the user chose on the source but that arrives as collateral on the target."

So the trigger is about *whose intent counts*, not about which machine runs commands. With that correction:

questions.question: Given that correction — the source's manual set is read only as evidence of intent, never acted on — should D-30's collateral prompt keep consulting it? Concretely: apt on the target wants to remove Y to satisfy an approved install; Y is auto-installed on the target but manually installed on the source.

options.label: Keep consulting both sets (Recommended)
options.description: Ask before removing Y. It costs nothing extra at runtime — the source's showmanual set is already captured as the manifest — and it catches the case where a package you deliberately chose on the source gets silently deleted from the target just because it landed there as a dependency. This is today's behaviour and ADR-020's stated reason for it.

options.label: Target's manual set only
options.description: Only ask when Y is manually installed on the TARGET. Simpler rule, and defensible: if the target auto-installed Y, the target's apt owns it. Cost: a package you hand-picked on the source can vanish from the target with no prompt, because the target never recorded it as chosen.

options.label: Skip-always set only, per ruling 3
options.description: Narrowest — ask only when Y is marked machine-specific on the target. One consistent rule for every follow-up prompt in the run. Cost: apt can silently remove manually-installed packages on either machine that were never explicitly marked.

questions.question: You've put /etc/apt/apt.conf.d back to reviewed in both directions. Pins (/etc/apt/preferences.d) are the other non-package /etc/apt class — but they MUST always sync for origin replication to work at all (Ubuntu's firefox is epoch 1:, so the Mozilla repo alone loses without its pin). What about pin REMOVAL — a pin deleted on the source, still present on the target?

options.label: Reviewed, two-way like repo removals (Recommended)
options.description: Pin additions and updates always sync silently (they must, or origins don't replicate). Pin REMOVAL gets a review line with remove or skip-once, no registry — the same shape you chose for repositories. Deleting a pin is destructive: it can flip which vendor's package the target installs on the next upgrade.

options.label: Always sync, removals included
options.description: Pins mirror the source completely and silently, in both directions. Simplest and most predictable — /etc/apt/preferences.d just matches. But a pin deletion can silently change which vendor supplies a package on the target's next upgrade, with nothing shown.

options.label: Reviewed in both directions, like apt.conf.d
options.description: Consistent with the choice you just made for apt.conf.d: pins get review lines for add, change and remove. But it means an approved package whose origin needs a pin could have that pin left unticked — reintroducing exactly the "package ticked, its source unticked" inconsistency that derived repos exist to make unrepresentable.
